title: Relativistic Algebra over Finite Ring Continuum

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: Completeness is primality: the residues of a count $q\ge2$ have no proper nonzero ideal exactly when $q$ is prime, so $\Fp$ is a field.
rows.name: completeness_is_primality

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: The quarter-turn criterion: for an odd prime $\p$, $-1$ is a square in $\Fp$ exactly when $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ (Euler's criterion).
rows.name: quarter_turn_criterion

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: Primitive roots: $\Fpx$ is cyclic of order $\p-1$; every prime field has a primitive root $\gen$, with $\gen^{\p-1}=1$ and $\langle\gen\rangle=\Fpx$.
rows.name: prime_carries_frame

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: The shell, capacity-first: $\kap$ primary, $\p=4\kap+1$ prime; the frame $(\tau;0,1,\gen)$ with $\gen$ a primitive root and the drive $x\mapsto\gen x$; the cycle $\Phi_\p\cong C_{\p-1}$; $\im:=-\gen^{\kap}$, $-1=\gen^{2\kap}$.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: Symmetry completeness: the fourth roots of unity form the unique order-four subgroup $Q_4=\{1,\im,-1,-\im\}$; under the Klein four-group $\langle x\mapsto-x,\,x\mapsto x^{-1}\rangle$, $Q_4$ is the union of the two size-two orbits $\{\pm1\}$, $\{\pm\im\}$, and $\Fpx\setminus Q_4$ splits into exactly $\kap-1$ orbits of size four. For $\p\equiv3\pmod4$ no $\im$ exists.
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:symmetric-completeness}\newline \pywit{algebra}{p01004}{B2}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p01004}{B2}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p01004}{B2} \lean{Algebra.quarter\_turn\_exists, Algebra.klein\_orbit\_four, Algebra.card\_fourth\_roots, FRC.Shell.Frame.quarter\_turn\_exists, FRC.Shell.Frame.fourth\_roots, FRC.Shell.Frame.klein\_orbit\_four, FRC.Shell.Frame.orbit\_rep, FRC.Shell.Frame.orbit\_rep\_unique, FRC.Shell.s13\_klein}
rows.name: symmetry_completeness

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The oriented quarter-turn: $\im=-\gen^{\kap}$ satisfies $\im^{2}=-1$ for every primitive root $\gen$; the two square roots of $-1$ are $\{-\gen^{\kap},\gen^{\kap}\}$, so the drive fixes which is $\im$. On $\F_{13}$, $\gen=2$: $\im=5$.
rows.name: oriented_quarter_turn

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: Affine reframing: $\varphi_{a,b}(x)=a+bx$, $b\neq0$, is a ring isomorphism $(\Fp,+,\cdot)\to(\Fp,\oplus,\otimes)$ with origin $a$ and unit $a+b$; every polynomial identity is frame-covariant.
rows.name: affine_reframing

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: Origin and unit are observer data (affine gauge); the generator $\gen$ is the frame's drive, not gauge; the observer's window is the naturals below $\sqrt\p$.

blocks.title: Arithmetic symmetries and the orbital complex

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: The four symmetries as maps of the shell: the successor $C_1:k\mapsto k+1$; translations $T_a$, $a\in\Fp$, the cycle $C_\p$; scalings $S_m$, $m\in\Fpx$, the cycle $C_{\p-1}$; power maps $P_\varepsilon:x\mapsto x^{\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in C_{\p-1}$, bijective iff $\gcd(\varepsilon,\p-1)=1$.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: The frame group: $\langle T_a,S_m\rangle$ is the affine group of order $\p(\p-1)$, acting simply transitively on the frames $(a,b)$, $b\neq0$; the set of frames is a torsor under it.
rows.name: frame_group

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: Meridians and latitudes: $M_n(a)=a\gen^{n}$, $a\in\Fp$, the ordered list of the shell with step $\gen^{n}$; $L_a(m)=a\gen^{m}$, $m\in C_{\p-1}$, $a\neq0$, the multiplicative cycle from $a$; the orbital complex $\Sp$ with vertex set $\{(n,\pm a)\}\cup\{0\}$. The $2$-sphere reading is 2-geometry's~\cite{akhtman2025geometry}.

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: Involutions and counts: $M_n(a)=M_{n+2\kap}(-a)$ and $L_a(m)=L_{-a}(m+2\kap)$ since $\gen^{2\kap}=-1$; $\p-1$ distinct meridian lists in $2\kap$ great circles; $2\kap$ latitude pairs; one-sided vertex count $(\p-1)^{2}/2+1$, the double cover $(\p-1)^{2}$.
rows.source: Section~\ref{sec:sphere}, Def.~\ref{def:orbit-sphere}\newline \pywit{algebra}{p01011}{C4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p01011}{C4}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p01011}{C4} \lean{Algebra.meridian\_involution, FRC.Shell.Frame.meridian\_involution, FRC.Shell.Frame.pow\_inj, FRC.Shell.Frame.sign\_pair, FRC.Shell.Frame.window\_injective, FRC.Shell.Frame.window\_signed, FRC.Shell.Frame.vertex\_count}
rows.name: involutions_and_counts

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: Framed integers: the window $W_H=\{z\in\Z:|z|\le H\}$, $2H<\p$, embedded by $z\mapsto z\bmod\p$; sign, order and magnitude are the window's; sums read back for $4H<\p$, products for $2H^{2}<\p$.

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: The window law: $z\mapsto z\bmod\p$ is injective on $W_H$ when $2H<\p$; for $x,y\in W_H$ the residue of $x\pm y$ reads back the integer when $4H<\p$, and that of $xy$ when $2H^{2}<\p$ (the same injectivity on the windows $2H$ and $H^{2}$).
rows.name: window_law

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: Framed rationals: $a/b$ with $a,b\in W_H$, $b\not\equiv0$, of value $ab^{-1}\in\Fp$; the scale grid $[x,n]:=x\gen^{-n}$, $x\in\{0,\dots,\p-1\}$, $n\in C_{\p-1}$; $G_n$ the ordered list $(x\gen^{-n})_x$, the meridian $M_{-n}$ of C3.

rows.label: D8
rows.predicate: The window law for framed rationals: for $2ND<\p$, fractions $a/b$ with $|a|\le N$, $1\le b\le D$ and equal values are equal fractions; products of such fractions with $|a|,b\le H$ read back when $2H^{4}<\p$, sums when $4H^{4}<\p$.
rows.name: window_law_framed_rationals

rows.label: D9
rows.predicate: The scale grid covers the field: for every unit $B$, every element of $\Fp$ is $tB^{-1}$ for exactly one integer $t$ with $|t|\le2\kap$; each grid $\{t/\gen^{n}\}$ lists every element once.
rows.name: scale_grid_covers_field

rows.label: D4
rows.predicate: Scale-periodicity, in the field: $S_n(x)=x\gen^{-n}$ satisfies $S_{n+(\p-1)}=S_n$, and the period is exact: for $x\neq0$, $x\gen^{-m}=x\gen^{-n}$ iff $m\equiv n\pmod{\p-1}$; each grid $G_n$ lists every residue once; the zoom has order $\p-1$. As lists of rationals $x/\gen^{n}$ the grids are not periodic.
rows.source: Lem.~\ref{thm:scale-periodicity}; 6:D4\newline \pywit{algebra}{p01015}{D4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p01015}{D4}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p01015}{D4} \lean{Algebra.scale\_periodic, FRC.Shell.Frame.scale\_periodic, FRC.Shell.Frame.scale\_inv\_periodic, FRC.Shell.Frame.scale\_exact, FRC.Shell.Frame.zoom\_order, FRC.Shell.Frame.scale\_bijective}
rows.name: scale_periodicity_field

rows.label: D6
rows.predicate: The continuum as chart: the framed real line is the reading of the nested grids against $\R$, a labelled idealisation entered nowhere as an object; no completion, compactness or ``complete continuum'' is claimed.

blocks.title: The complex chart, polynomial equations and continuous symmetry

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: The framed complex chart: the pair $(a,b)\in W_H^{2}$ read as $a+b\im\in\Fp$; the quarter-turn acts on the shell as the rotation $x\mapsto\im x$ of order four; the chart is the plane picture of $Q_4$ acting on the shell, not an extension of $\Fp$.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: The extension by $X^{2}+1$ is trivial: on the shell $\Fp[X]/(X^{2}+1)$ has zero divisors, $(X+\im)(X-\im)=0$, so it is not a field; $\Fp[X]/(X^{2}+1)$ is a field exactly when $\p\equiv3\pmod4$, every nonzero pair $(a,b)$ having the inverse $(a,-b)/(a^{2}+b^{2})$.
rows.name: quadratic_extension_trivial

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: Solving in the substrate: $f\in\Fp[X]$ has a root in $\Fp$ iff $f$ and $X^{\p}-X=\prod_{a}(X-a)$ are not coprime; a nonzero $f$ of degree $d$ has at most $d$ roots. An equation without a root in $\Fp$ is recognised, not extended (E2).
rows.name: solving_substrate

rows.label: E4
rows.predicate: Continuous symmetry, the abelian case: $\Fpx\simeq C_{\p-1}$ is a $\pi/(\p-1)$-net of $U(1)$ under $k\mapsto e^{2\pi\im k/(\p-1)}$; the rounding of a framed turn $u/v$ to $C_{\p-1}$ lies within half a step, and its group-law defect is at most one step.
rows.name: continuous_symmetry_abelian

rows.label: Z1
rows.predicate: No element of additive order two: $2s=0$ forces $s=0$; the antipode of the origin on the additive cycle is not a residue; it sits between $2\kap=(\p-1)/2$ and $2\kap+1=(\p+1)/2=2^{-1}$.
rows.name: no_additive_order_two

rows.label: Z2
rows.predicate: The antipode, charted $\infty$: the compactification point of the framed line beyond the observer's horizon; its reading as classical infinity is the chart, not a residue.

rows.label: Z3
rows.predicate: No latitude on the equator: $4s=0$ forces $s=0$; a framed rational at a quarter position of the additive cycle ($\p/4$, $\p/2$, $3\p/4$) has value $0$, and none of the window sits there; the equator, depth $\kap+\tfrac14$, lies strictly between $L_\kap$ and $L_{\kap+1}$.
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:no-equator}\newline \pywit{algebra}{p01034}{Z3}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p01034}{Z3}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p01034}{Z3} \lean{Algebra.no\_equator, Algebra.quarter\_position, Algebra.quarter\_position\_window, Algebra.equator\_between, FRC.Shell.Frame.no\_equator, FRC.Shell.Frame.quarter\_fold, FRC.Shell.Frame.quarter\_position, FRC.Shell.Frame.equator\_between}
rows.name: no_latitude_equator

legend.name: Definition
legend.text: A naming or declared convention, carrying no empirical content.

legend.name: Theorem
legend.text: Derived, and machine-verified in exact arithmetic by the named witness.

A1.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.isPrime_iff_complete
A1.doc: 1:A1, 7:A23, Completeness is primality, in the ideal form (A10): for `p ≥ 2`, every ideal of the shell that holds a nonzero residue holds every residue iff `p` is prime. An ideal `I` holds `0` and is closed under addition and under multiplication by any residue. Forward, a nonzero `a ∈ I` has the inverse `a^{p−2}` (Fermat), so `1 ∈ I` and then `x = x · 1 ∈ I`. Backward, the annihilator `{x : x b = 0}` of `b` is an ideal, so `a b = 0` with `a ≠ 0` puts `1` in it and `b = 0`: no zero divisors, so `p` is prime.

A2.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.quarter_turn_iff
A2.doc: 1:A2, the quarter-turn criterion on a prime `p > 2`: `x² = −1` is solvable iff `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`. Forward, `ħ⁴ = 1` and `ħ^{(p−1) mod 4} = 1` leave only `(p − 1) mod 4 = 0`; backward, the chart.

A3.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.exists_drive
A3.doc: 1:A3, 00:A12, 26:E10, 26:F10 — every prime carries a frame: the prime shell `𝔽_p` has a drive `g`, a primitive root of order `p − 1`, and its powers `g^m`, `m < p − 1`, reach every nonzero residue (`⟨g⟩ = 𝔽_p^×`, the pigeonhole).

B2.name: FRC.Algebra.quarter_turn_exists
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, existence clause): on the shell `card F = 4κ+1` a quarter-turn `u` with `u² = −1` exists. Mathlib: `FiniteField.isSquare_neg_one_iff`.

B2.name: FRC.Algebra.klein_orbit_four
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, orbit clause), 2:D7: for a unit `x` with `x² ≠ 1` and `x² ≠ −1` the four elements `x, −x, x⁻¹, −x⁻¹` of the Klein-four orbit are pairwise distinct (any field of characteristic `≠ 2`); the structural set `{1, i, −1, −i}` is exactly the complement.

B2.name: FRC.Algebra.card_fourth_roots
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, the structural set): the fourth roots of unity number exactly `4` on the shell. Mathlib: `IsPrimitiveRoot.card_rootsOfUnity`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.quarter_turn_exists
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, existence clause) — a quarter-turn `u` with `u² = −1` exists on every shell.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.fourth_roots
B2.doc: 1:B2, 2:D2 (Theorem 1, the structural set) — the fourth roots of unity are exactly `1, −1, i, −i`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.klein_orbit_four
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1 of 1-algebra), 2:D7 — off the fourth roots of unity, `x`, `−x`, `x⁻¹`, `−x⁻¹` are four distinct residues (`y` stands for the inverse: `x·y = 1`).

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orbit_rep
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, the count, existence), 2:D7 — every residue off `Q₄` lies in the Klein orbit of some `g^r` with `1 ≤ r < κ`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orbit_rep_unique
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, the count, uniqueness), 2:D7 — two representatives `g^r`, `g^{r'}` with `1 ≤ r, r' < κ` whose orbits meet are the same: the Klein orbits off `Q₄` are exactly `κ − 1`, one for each `r ∈ [1, κ)`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.s13_klein
B2.doc: 1:B2 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃` the fourth roots of unity are `{1, 5, 12, 8}`, and every other nonzero residue has four distinct companions `{x, −x, x⁻¹, −x⁻¹}`: the two Klein orbits `{2, 11, 7, 6}` and `{3, 10, 9, 4}`.

B3.name: FRC.Algebra.quarter_turn
B3.doc: 1:B3 (convention 4, the oriented quarter-turn): `i := −g^κ` satisfies `i² = −1`; and `g^(2κ) = −1`, the involution behind Definition 5. From `FrcMathlib.Fourier`.

B3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.quarter_turn_sq
B3.doc: 1:B3, 2:D2, 13:J2 — the quarter-turn `i = −g^κ` squares to `−1` (the pinning relation `i² + 1 ≡ 0`).

B4.name: FRC.Algebra.affine_frame
B4.doc: 1:B4 (Definition 2, Lemma 1): in the affine frame `(a, b)`, `φ x = a + b x` carries `+` and `·` to `⊕` and `⊗`, is a bijection, and the multiplicative unit of the relabelled field is `a + b`; `b` is the unit only when `a = 0`.

B4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.affine_frame_unit
B4.doc: 1:B4 (Definition 2 of 1-algebra) — in the affine frame `(a, b)` the multiplicative unit is `a + b`, not `b`: `(a + b) ⊗ z = z` for every `z`.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.Affine.simply_transitive
C2.doc: 1:C2, 4:C5 (the frame group), simple transitivity — for frames `(a, b)` and `(c, d)` (`b, d ≠ 0`) there is exactly one affine map carrying the first to the second: `φ (a, b) := (φ.apply a, φ.b · b)`.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frame_count
C2.doc: 1:C2, 4:C5, the order — the frames `(a, b)`, `b ≠ 0`, number `p·(p − 1)`: `p` choices of the origin, `p − 1` of the unit.

C4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.pow_inj
C4.doc: 1:C4, 26:B3 — the powers `g⁰, …, g^{n−1}` of the drive are distinct: `g^i = g^j` with `i, j < n` forces `i = j`.

C4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.sign_pair
C4.doc: 1:C4 — the nonzero residues form `2κ` sign pairs: every `x ≠ 0` is `a` or `−a` for some `1 ≤ a ≤ 2κ` (the pair is unique by `window_injective` and `window_signed` at `H = 2κ`).

C4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.window_injective
C4.doc: 1:C4, 1:D2 (the window law, injectivity) — two window integers `x, y ≤ H` with `2H < p` that read as the same residue are equal: `ofNat x = ofNat y → x = y`. (Both are below `p`, so the residues are the integers.)

C4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.window_signed
C4.doc: 1:C4, 1:D2, the signed window: `x` and `−y` (`x, y ≤ H`, `2H < p`) read as the same residue only when both are zero — the window's positive and negative halves do not overlap.

C4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.vertex_count
C4.doc: 1:C4 — the one-sided vertex count: `(p − 1)² = 2 · (2κ · (p − 1))`, with `p − 1 = 4κ`; the orbital complex has `2κ(p − 1) + 1` vertices, half its double cover plus the origin.

D2.name: FRC.Algebra.framed_integer_window
D2.doc: 1:D2 (Definition 6 made precise): the framed-integer window. Integers of absolute value `≤ H` with `2H < card F` have distinct residues: the cast `ℤ → ZMod p` is injective on the window. Stated on `ZMod p`.

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.window_injective
D2.doc: 1:C4, 1:D2 (the window law, injectivity) — two window integers `x, y ≤ H` with `2H < p` that read as the same residue are equal: `ofNat x = ofNat y → x = y`. (Both are below `p`, so the residues are the integers.)

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.window_signed
D2.doc: 1:C4, 1:D2, the signed window: `x` and `−y` (`x, y ≤ H`, `2H < p`) read as the same residue only when both are zero — the window's positive and negative halves do not overlap.

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.window_add_readback
D2.doc: 1:D2, the read-back of sums: for `x, y ≤ H` and `4H < p`, the residue of `x + y` determines the integer `x + y` among the integers `z ≤ 2H`.

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.window_mul_readback
D2.doc: 1:D2, the read-back of products: for `x, y ≤ H` and `2H² < p`, the residue of `x·y` determines the integer `x·y` among the integers `z ≤ H²`.

D8.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frac_window
D8.doc: 1:D8, the window law for framed rationals — two fractions `a₁/b₁`, `a₂/b₂` with `|aᵢ| ≤ N`, `bᵢ ≤ D` and `2ND < p` whose cross-products agree on the shell, `a₁ b₂ ≡ a₂ b₁`, are the same fraction: `a₁ b₂ = a₂ b₁` as integers.

D8.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frac_window_inv
D8.doc: 1:D8, in the residues of the fractions — `a₁ · b₁⁻¹ = a₂ · b₂⁻¹` on the shell, with the window bounds and `2ND < p`, forces `a₁ b₂ = a₂ b₁`: distinct window fractions take distinct residues.

D8.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frac_mul_readback
D8.doc: 1:D8, products read back — for window fractions `a/b`, `c/d` (`|a|, |c|, b, d ≤ H`) the product `ac/bd` lies in the window `(H², H²)`; when `2H⁴ < p` the residue of the product determines it among that window's fractions `e/f`.

D8.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frac_add_readback
D8.doc: 1:D8, sums read back — for window fractions `a/b`, `c/d` the sum `(ad + cb)/bd` lies in the window `(2H², H²)`; when `4H⁴ < p` its residue determines it among that window's fractions `e/f`.

D9.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.signed_rep
D9.doc: 1:D9 — every residue of the shell `p = 4κ + 1` is the reading of exactly one signed window integer of size `2κ` (existence here, uniqueness `signed_rep_unique`).

D9.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.signed_rep_unique
D9.doc: 1:D9, uniqueness — two signed window integers of size `2κ` with the same reading are equal.

D9.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.grid_cover
D9.doc: 1:D9 — for every unit `B` (`B · y = 1`) the scale grid `t · B⁻¹`, `|t| ≤ 2κ`, covers the shell.

D9.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.grid_unique
D9.doc: 1:D9 — and each residue sits on the grid once: `t · B⁻¹ = t' · B⁻¹` with `|t|, |t'| ≤ 2κ` forces `t = t'`.

D4.name: FRC.Algebra.scale_periodic
D4.doc: 1:D4 (Lemma 2 restated in the field — scale-periodicity): the scale map `S n x = x · g^(−n)` on the shell is `(card F − 1)`-periodic in `n`: the residue grids `G_n = S_n(0..p−1)` coincide as ordered lists.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.scale_periodic
D4.doc: 1:D4 (Lemma 2 of 1-algebra, scale periodicity) — the residue grid repeats with the period `p − 1` of the drive: `g^{n + (p−1)} = g^n`, hence `x·g^{n + (p−1)} = x·g^n` for every `x`.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.scale_inv_periodic
D4.doc: 1:D4 — the grid of scale `n` is periodic in `n` with period `p − 1`: `x · y^{n+(p−1)} = x · y^n`.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.scale_exact
D4.doc: 1:D4, the period is exact — for a nonzero `x` the grid points `x · y^m` and `x · y^n` coincide exactly when `m ≡ n (mod p − 1)`: no smaller shift of scale returns a nonzero point to its place.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.zoom_order
D4.doc: 1:D4, the zoom has order `p − 1` — the zoom by `k` steps fixes every grid point, `x · y^k = x` for all `x`, exactly when `(p − 1) ∣ k`.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.scale_bijective
D4.doc: 1:D4, every grid is the whole shell — the scale map `x ↦ x · y^n` is onto (`z = (z g^n) y^n`) and one-to-one, so each grid `G_n` lists every residue once, and `G_m`, `G_n` are equal as ordered lists exactly when `m ≡ n (mod p − 1)` (`scale_exact` at `x = 1`, `scale_inv_periodic`).

E2.name: FRC.Algebra.complex_chart_zero_divisor
E2.doc: 1:E2 (Proposition 5 reversed): adjoining a root of `X² + 1` to a field that already contains one gives zero divisors — `F[X]/(X²+1)` is not a field on the shell. With `u² = −1`, `(X + u)(X − u) = 0` in the quotient while both factors are nonzero.

E2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.complex_chart_zero_divisor
E2.doc: 1:E2 (Proposition 5 reversed) — on a shell that already has a square root of `−1` the complex chart is not a field: `(i, 1)·(−i, 1) = (0, 0)` with both factors nonzero (`X + i` and `X − i` are zero divisors).

E2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.complex_chart_field
E2.doc: 1:E2, the converse — on a prime `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` the chart `F_p[X]/(X² + 1)` is a field: every nonzero pair `(a, b)` has the inverse `(a, −b)/(a² + b²)`, since `a² + b² = 0` with `b ≠ 0` would make `a/b` a square root of `−1`.

E3.name: FRC.Algebra.root_iff_not_coprime
E3.doc: 1:E3 (the conjecture's first clause, solving): `f ∈ F_p[X]` has a root in `F_p` iff `f` and `X^p − X = ∏_a (X − a)` are not coprime — the root test is a gcd, exact in the substrate.

E3.name: FRC.Shell.Poly.Frame.root_iff_common_factor
E3.doc: 1:E3, the root criterion — `f` has a root in the shell iff `f` and `X^p − X` share a factor of positive degree. Forward: the factor is `X − a` (synthetic division, Fermat). Backward: a common factor `d` of degree `m ≥ 1` with no root would force its cofactor in `X^p − X`, of degree `p − m < p`, to vanish at all `p` residues, hence to be zero (`root_bound`), against `X^p − X ≠ 0`; the root of `d` is found by deciding `∃ i < p, d(i) = 0`.

E3.name: FRC.Shell.Poly.Frame.root_bound
E3.doc: 1:E3, the root bound — a polynomial of degree at most `n` that vanishes at `n + 1` distinct points is zero: the distinct roots are counted by the degree.

E3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.fermat
E3.doc: 1:E3, the finitary core (Fermat): every residue satisfies `x^p = x` — the polynomial `X^p − X` vanishes on the whole shell, which is what the root test of 1:E3 rests on.

E4.name: FRC.Algebra.circle_net
E4.doc: 1:E4 (third clause, the abelian case): the rounding `k(θ) = round(Nθ/2π)` puts `2πk/N` within `π/N` of `θ` — `C_N ≅ F_p^×` (`N = p − 1`) is a `π/N`-net of `U(1)`.

E4.name: FRC.Algebra.group_law_defect
E4.doc: 1:E4 (third clause): the group-law defect of the rounding is at most one step.

E4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.round_exists
E4.doc: 1:E4, 2:E2, 2:E4 — every framed turn has its rounding (the division with remainder by `2v`).

E4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.round_defect
E4.doc: 1:E4 — the rounding's group-law defect is `−1`, `0` or `1`: `k(u) + k(u′)` and `k(u + u′)` differ by at most one step of the cycle.

Z1.name: FRC.Algebra.no_south_pole
Z1.doc: 1:Z1 (Theorem 3): `2s = 0 ⇒ s = 0` in a field of characteristic `≠ 2`: the additive cycle has no element of order two; the antipode of the origin is not a residue.

Z1.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.no_south_pole
Z1.doc: 1:Z1 (Theorem 3) — `2s = 0 ⇒ s = 0`: the additive cycle has no element of order two; the antipode of the origin is not a residue.

Z3.name: FRC.Algebra.no_equator
Z3.doc: 1:Z3 (Theorem thm:no-equator): `4s = 0 ⇒ s = 0` in a field of characteristic `≠ 2`: the additive cycle has no element of order four; the quarter positions of the cycle are no residues.

Z3.name: FRC.Algebra.quarter_position
Z3.doc: 1:Z3 — a framed rational `a/b` at a quarter position of the additive cycle, `a/b = p(4n+j)/4` with `j ∈ {1, 2, 3}`, satisfies `4a = p·b·(4n+j)` as integers; on the shell this forces `a ≡ 0`, so its value `a b⁻¹` is `0`. Stated for every integer `m` in place of `4n + j`.

Z3.name: FRC.Algebra.quarter_position_window
Z3.doc: 1:Z3 — no framed rational of a window `W_H`, `2H < p`, sits at a quarter position: `4a = p·b·m` with `b, m ≠ 0` and `|a| ≤ H` is impossible, since `p ∣ a` and `|a| < p` force `a = 0`.

Z3.name: FRC.Algebra.equator_between
Z3.doc: 1:Z3 — the equator lies strictly between the latitudes `L_κ` and `L_{κ+1}`: `4κ < p < 4(κ + 1)` on `p = 4κ + 1`.

Z3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.no_equator
Z3.doc: 1:Z3 (Theorem thm:no-equator) — `4s = 0 ⇒ s = 0`: the additive cycle has no element of order four; the quarter positions of the cycle (the equator crossings and the antipode) are no residues.

Z3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.quarter_fold
Z3.doc: 1:Z3 — the quarter fold: `4κ = −1` on the shell (`4κ = p − 1`), so the equator's depth `κ + 1/4 = p/4` has the value `0` and `κ = −4⁻¹`, `κ + 1 = 3·4⁻¹` (restated as 8:F2 `four_kappa` downstream).

Z3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.quarter_position
Z3.doc: 1:Z3 — a fraction at a quarter position of the additive cycle: `4a = p·m` as naturals (the position `a/b` of a framed rational is `p(4n+j)/4` with `j ∈ {1,2,3}`, so `4a = p·b·(4n+j)`) forces the residue of `a`, hence the value `a b⁻¹`, to be `0`.

Z3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.equator_between
Z3.doc: 1:Z3 — the equator lies strictly between the latitudes `L_κ` and `L_{κ+1}`: `4κ < p < 4(κ + 1)`.
